findings.title: External authority anchor is not snapshotted before the authority callback
evidence: The callback is invoked exactly once.
A valid but untrusted anchor present at entry can be replaced inside read_completion_material and the result is accepted as completed.
A hostile expected_registry_anchor proxy throws before the sanitized authority-read boundary.
findings.impact: The completed decision can depend on mutable post-entry authority bytes instead of one immutable externally owned authority snapshot.

findings.title: Canonicalization has no structural depth or size bound
evidence: A 25000-level request structure raises an uncaught recursion error instead of a deterministic fail-closed result.
Cycles, ordinary accessors and hostile observed-material proxies are otherwise sanitized.
findings.impact: Extreme caller-controlled structures can escape the contract boundary and create an availability failure.

findings.title: Semantically identical reordered gap closures drift the completed result digest
evidence: Canonical and reversed closure arrays both return completed.
Both close the same exact 18 gap codes.
findings.impact: The contract does not provide byte-identical input-order determinism for the 18-closure evidence set.

findings.title: Early registry rejection labels nested observed row and bundle sections absent
evidence: The verified completion_material digest still binds the nested bytes.
The repository_row and evidence_bundle provenance sections remain disposition absent when an invalid registry stops parsing.
findings.impact: Failure identities remain input-distinct through the material digest, but per-section forensic disposition is less precise than the observed input.
